problem: 2D detectors ignore z-continuity, causing flicker false positives across slices.
hyp: Predicting slice z-position and ordering as pretext learns anatomy priors that stabilize per-slice detections.
why: Free supervision from every volume; no labels needed.
novel: Uses z-ordering itself, not contrastive slabs, as anatomical supervision signal.
min_exp: Pretrain on LIDC ordering task; measure inter-slice detection flicker and FROC vs scratch.
risk: Ordering may be too easy, learning trivial cues.

problem: Sharp vs soft reconstruction kernels change texture; detectors fail across kernels.
hyp: Paired reconstructions of the same raw scan enforce kernel invariance better than style augmentation.
why: Many archives store dual-kernel recons; real paired data exists.
novel: Exploits physically paired recons instead of synthetic domain augmentation.
min_exp: Train with kernel-pair consistency loss on dual-recon dataset; test cross-kernel lesion sensitivity.
risk: Paired-kernel archives limited to few vendors.

problem: Resampling anisotropic CT/MRI to isotropic grids blurs thin lesions.
hyp: Conditioning convolutions on physical voxel spacing outperforms resampling for variable-thickness data.
why: Slice thickness varies 0.5-5mm clinically; resampling destroys detail.
novel: Treats spacing as continuous network input, not preprocessing target.
min_exp: Compare spacing-conditioned vs resampled nnU-Net on mixed-thickness lesion set.
risk: Marginal gain if thickness distribution narrow.

problem: 4D CT lesion tracking drifts across respiratory phases.
hyp: Enforcing cycle-closure (phase 0→50→0 returns identity) regularizes deformation and lesion tracking.
why: Respiration is periodic; closure is a free physical constraint.
novel: Uses respiratory periodicity as loss, unlike generic registration smoothness.
min_exp: 4D-CT lung dataset; measure tracking error with vs without cycle loss.

problem: MRI lesions subtle in single sequences; registration errors corrupt fusion.
hyp: Voxelwise disagreement between T1/T2/FLAIR predictions, after uncertainty gating, localizes lesions better than channel concatenation.
why: Pathology alters sequences differently; disagreement is diagnostic.
novel: Treats inter-sequence prediction conflict as feature, not noise.
min_exp: BraTS: compare disagreement-map detector vs concatenated-input baseline.

problem: Lesion boundary voxels are tissue mixtures; hard labels mistrain edges.
hyp: Modeling boundary voxels as explicit two-tissue mixtures, supervised by thin-slice recons, improves volumetry.
why: Volumetric accuracy drives treatment response scoring.
novel: Sub-voxel supervision from paired thin/thick reconstructions of same scan.
min_exp: Downsample thin-slice CT; predict mixture fractions; evaluate volume error.

problem: Longitudinal lesion comparison needs brittle deformable registration.
hyp: Anatomy-anchored tokens (vessel bifurcations, vertebrae) allow correspondence-level change detection without dense registration.
why: Follow-up comparison is the dominant radiology task.
novel: Sparse anatomical token matching replaces dense deformation fields.
min_exp: Paired baseline/follow-up CTs; detect grown nodules vs registration-based pipeline.

problem: 3D detector confidence poorly calibrated; no unsupervised quality signal.
hyp: Variance of per-slice detections along z (flicker) predicts false positives without labels.
why: True lesions persist across slices; artifacts do not.
novel: Repurposes temporal-smoothness ideas as label-free calibration in anatomical z-axis.
min_exp: Correlate flicker score with FP/TP status on LUNA16 outputs.
risk: Small lesions span one slice legitimately.

problem: WSI models trained at one magnification fail at others.
hyp: Forcing 10x features to predict pooled 20x context yields magnification-equivariant representations.
why: Scanners and labs use different objectives; equivariance transfers.
novel: Distillation across pyramid levels of the same slide, no extra data.
min_exp: Train on 20x, test mitosis detection at 10x/40x vs baseline.
risk: Optical blur differences not purely scale.

problem: RGB color jitter poorly models real stain variation.
hyp: Augmenting hematoxylin/eosin channels in Beer-Lambert optical-density space matches inter-lab shifts better than RGB jitter.
why: Stain physics is multiplicative in transmittance, linear in OD.
novel: Physically parameterized augmentation grounded in stain chemistry.
min_exp: Camelyon cross-center test: OD augmentation vs HED-light vs RGB jitter.
risk: Gains may duplicate existing stain-norm tools.

problem: Hard WSI examples expensive to find in gigapixel slides.
hyp: Regions where level-0 and level-1 predictions disagree are enriched for boundary and hard cases.
why: Consistency across pyramid is necessary for correctness.
novel: Uses the stored pyramid itself as a free ensemble for mining.
min_exp: Active-learning loop selecting disagreement patches; compare label efficiency.
risk: Disagreement dominated by trivial blur regions.

problem: Tissue folds, pen marks, bubbles trigger tumor false positives.
hyp: Self-supervised artifact segmentation (artifacts are synthesizable) pretrains features that improve tumor detection robustness.
why: Artifacts are lab-independent, abundant, and rule-generable.
novel: Artifacts as pretext target rather than nuisance to filter.
min_exp: Synthesize folds/marks, pretrain, fine-tune Camelyon; measure FP on artifact slides.

problem: Scanner focus varies spatially; blur degrades mitosis detection unevenly.
hyp: Predicting a per-region focus map and conditioning the detector recovers accuracy in soft-focus zones.
why: Focus failures cluster by scanner and slide position.
novel: Explicit focus estimation as detector input, not slide-level QC reject.
min_exp: MIDOG: add focus head; compare recall in blurred quartile.

problem: Sparse WSI annotations propagate poorly via rectangular patch grids.
hyp: Propagating labels along a tissue-contiguity graph (superpixel adjacency within tissue) beats grid-based pseudo-labeling.
why: Tumor grows along tissue structures, not pixel grids.
novel: Graph respects histologic architecture instead of raster tiles.
min_exp: 10% annotation Camelyon; graph propagation vs grid pseudo-labels.
risk: Graph construction cost at gigapixel scale.

problem: WSI micron-per-pixel metadata is sometimes wrong or missing.
hyp: Lymphocyte nuclei (~7µm, biologically constant) serve as internal rulers to estimate and correct magnification.
why: Size-dependent tasks (nuclear grading) silently fail with bad metadata.
novel: Biological constant as self-calibration standard.
min_exp: Corrupt mpp metadata; recover via lymphocyte detector; measure grading recovery.

problem: Microtome section thickness varies, shifting stain density and confusing grading.
hyp: Estimating section thickness from background optical density enables per-slide density normalization improving cross-lab grading.
why: Thickness is unrecorded yet systematically varies by technician.
novel: Treats thickness as recoverable latent, not random noise.
min_exp: Serial sections at known thickness; predict thickness, normalize, test grading transfer.

problem: Electrocautery smoke blinds surgical tool detectors intermittently.
hyp: Estimating smoke density with a scattering (dehazing-style) prior and gating temporal memory by visibility reduces track loss.
why: Smoke is transient; memory should coast, not update.
novel: Visibility-gated memory driven by physical density estimate.
min_exp: CholecT50 smoky segments: tracking persistence with vs without gating.
risk: Density estimate fails under mixed smoke/blur.

problem: Specularities are treated as noise and inpainted away.
hyp: Under the endoscope's point light, highlight motion encodes surface normals, enabling tool-tissue contact detection.
why: Contact events matter for skill assessment and safety.
novel: Exploits co-located light-camera geometry unique to endoscopy.
min_exp: Label contact frames; classify from highlight-motion features vs RGB baseline.

problem: Irrigation floods the scene, silently corrupting trackers and phase models.
hyp: Detecting wash onset as a discrete event and resetting tracker priors outperforms treating frames uniformly.
why: Washes are frequent, stereotyped, globally disruptive.
novel: Event-structured video pipeline vs frame-uniform processing.
min_exp: Annotate wash events in Cholec80; compare phase accuracy around events.

problem: Tool segmentation confuses reflective tissue with metal instruments.
hyp: Tools move rigidly, tissue deforms; decomposing optical flow into rigid vs non-rigid components segments tools without appearance labels.
why: Motion rigidity is appearance-invariant across instruments.
novel: Rigidity as primary segmentation signal, not auxiliary.
min_exp: Unsupervised rigid-flow clustering vs supervised baseline on EndoVis.
risk: Stationary tools invisible to motion cues.

problem: Brightness varies with lens-tissue distance, confounding tissue classification.
hyp: Fitting a per-frame inverse-square illumination model and normalizing improves invariance to camera distance.
why: Falloff is deterministic physics, learnable exactly.
novel: Explicit photometric endoscope model instead of brightness augmentation.
min_exp: Distance-swept phantom footage; classify tissue with/without normalization.

problem: Pooled blood recolors tissue, causing organ misclassification.
hyp: Jointly segmenting blood film thickness and underlying tissue disentangles albedo shift, recovering organ labels.
why: Bleeding is constant in surgery; models silently degrade.
novel: Layered blood-over-tissue decomposition, not blood-as-class.
min_exp: Synthesize blood overlays on clean frames; test recovery; validate on real bleeding clips.

problem: Appearance-based phase recognition overfits to lighting and anatomy.
hyp: A learned automaton over tool co-occurrence transitions recognizes phases more robustly than frame appearance.
why: Surgical workflow is procedural; grammar transfers across hospitals.
novel: Symbolic transition structure learned from detections, appearance-free.
min_exp: Cross-hospital Cholec80 transfer: grammar model vs video transformer.

problem: Surgical videos contain out-of-body segments violating privacy and corrupting training.
hyp: Detecting scope insertion/retraction signatures (defocus, luminance collapse, trocar texture) segments videos automatically and reliably.
why: Out-of-body frames leak faces and staff identity.
novel: Uses optical insertion signature rather than generic scene classification.
min_exp: Label insertion events; test boundary accuracy vs frame classifier.

problem: Lens fogging degrades vision gradually until surgeon must withdraw scope.
hyp: Condensation onset cues (contrast slope, halo growth) predict fog seconds ahead, enabling preemptive alerts.
why: Forecasting beats detection; interruptions cost surgical time.
novel: Predictive quality degradation model, not post-hoc quality scoring.
min_exp: Timestamp fog events; ROC of 5-second-ahead prediction.

problem: Ultrasound speckle is discarded as noise, wasting microstructure signal.
hyp: Beam-steered compound frames of the same tissue form natural contrastive pairs; decorrelation rate encodes scatterer microstructure.
why: Compounding data exists on every modern scanner.
novel: Speckle statistics as self-supervision, not denoising target.
min_exp: Pretrain on steered-pair contrast; fine-tune thyroid nodule classification.

problem: Sonographers adjust time-gain sliders, creating depth-dependent gain shifts models never see.
hyp: Augmenting with realistic piecewise TGC curves beats global gamma/brightness jitter for cross-operator robustness.
why: TGC is the dominant operator-controlled appearance factor.
novel: Depth-structured, control-panel-faithful augmentation.
min_exp: Train with TGC augmentation; test across operators on breast ultrasound.
risk: True TGC settings unlogged for validation.

problem: Acoustic shadows are suppressed as artifacts, discarding diagnostic evidence.
hyp: Jointly detecting caster (stone, calcification) and its shadow as a geometric pair improves both precision and recall.
why: Radiologists explicitly use shadowing as a sign.
novel: Artifact and cause detected as coupled object pair.
min_exp: Gallstone dataset: paired head vs caster-only detection.
risk: Shadow geometry varies with probe angle.

problem: Lesion stiffness needs elastography hardware many clinics lack.
hyp: Natural probe-pressure oscillations in routine cine loops reveal relative stiffness via deformation amplitude, enabling stiffness-aware lesion detection.
why: Free stiffness signal in existing B-mode loops.
novel: Uncontrolled hand pressure as elastography source.
min_exp: Correlate flow-derived strain maps with elastography ground truth on breast lesions.

problem: Speckle tracking silently fails when tissue moves out of the imaging plane.
hyp: Speckle decorrelation rate predicts out-of-plane probability, giving trackers a principled abstain signal.
why: Silent tracking failure corrupts strain and lesion measurements.
novel: Decorrelation-calibrated abstention, not generic confidence.
min_exp: 3D-probe ground truth motion; calibrate decorrelation-to-elevation mapping.

problem: Scan conversion to Cartesian interpolates and distorts, especially at depth.
hyp: Detecting in native polar (beam-sample) coordinates with spacing-aware convolutions outperforms scan-converted input.
why: Resolution is beam-structured; Cartesian resampling loses it.
novel: Transducer-native geometry as the learning domain.
min_exp: Cardiac view: same architecture polar vs Cartesian, compare landmark accuracy.
risk: Polar data unavailable in public sets.

problem: Mirror and reverberation artifacts create phantom organs that fool detectors.
hyp: Predicting artifact geometry from detected strong reflectors (diaphragm, pleura) suppresses duplicated structures.
why: Artifact geometry is deterministic given the reflector.
novel: Forward physical artifact model integrated into suppression, not learned blindly.
min_exp: Liver scans: mirror-artifact FP rate with/without geometric suppression.

problem: Raw OCT intensity conflates reflectivity with overlying attenuation.
hyp: Depth-resolved attenuation-coefficient maps as an input channel improve fluid and drusen detection over intensity alone.
why: Attenuation is tissue-intrinsic; intensity is context-dependent.
novel: Physics-derived channel replacing learned normalization.
min_exp: AMD OCT set: add attenuation channel; compare fluid detection AUC.
risk: Attenuation estimation noisy in shadowed A-scans.

problem: Retinal vessel shadows corrupt OCT layer segmentation beneath them.
hyp: Detecting shadows via en-face vessel maps and inpainting A-scans restores layer continuity better than smoothness priors.
why: Shadow errors bias thickness maps used for glaucoma.
novel: Cross-view (en-face to B-scan) shadow reasoning.
min_exp: Layer accuracy under vessels: inpainting vs graph-cut smoothness.

problem: Fundus lesion labels are coarse; OCT holds precise pathology but different view.
hyp: Registering via vessel bifurcation graphs lets OCT-derived labels supervise fundus detectors pixel-accurately.
why: Paired fundus-OCT exams are routine; labels transfer free.
novel: Topological graph registration instead of intensity registration across modalities.
min_exp: Project OCT fluid onto fundus; train detector; validate against graders.

problem: Retinal disease priors are radially organized around fovea, but models use Cartesian grids.
hyp: Log-polar resampling centered on fovea encodes eccentricity priors, improving grading with fewer samples.
why: ETDRS grid — the clinical standard — is radial.
novel: Clinical grid geometry built into representation.
min_exp: Diabetic retinopathy grading: polar vs Cartesian at 10% data.

problem: Eye saccades cause axial and lateral jumps between B-scans, corrupting volumes.
hyp: Enforcing en-face vessel continuity detects and corrects inter-B-scan motion better than cross-correlation.
why: Motion artifacts limit home-OCT and pediatric imaging.
novel: Uses vasculature as intrinsic motion fiducial.
min_exp: Simulate jumps in clean volumes; measure correction accuracy; test downstream thickness maps.

problem: Models infer eye laterality from optic-disc position and exploit dataset laterality-disease correlations.
hyp: Disc-centric alignment (canonicalizing disc position) removes the shortcut, changing external-set performance measurably.
why: Laterality imbalance is common yet unaudited in fundus sets.
novel: Shortcut audit specific to ocular geometry.
min_exp: Compare flipped-input prediction consistency before/after canonicalization on EyePACS.

problem: Media opacity blurs fundus images; models conflate opacity with retinopathy severity.
hyp: Estimating opacity as an explicit latent and conditioning grading on it separates optical degradation from retinal pathology.
why: Elderly screening populations have high cataract prevalence.
novel: Degradation as declared covariate, not augmentation target.
min_exp: Pre/post cataract-surgery pairs: grading consistency with vs without conditioning.

problem: Mitosis phases form a temporal cycle, but static classifiers treat them as unordered classes.
hyp: Constraining phase embeddings onto a learned cycle (prophase through telophase) improves rare-phase recall.
why: Cycle structure is biological ground truth, free regularization.
novel: Topological (circular) label structure in histology classification.
min_exp: MIDOG phase labels: cyclic embedding vs softmax on rare phases.

problem: Apoptotic and necrotic nuclei mimic mitoses, dominating detector false positives.
hyp: Mining hard negatives via nuclear-fragmentation descriptors (karyorrhexis patterns) reduces FPs more than random negatives.
why: Mitotic count directly determines tumor grade.
novel: Biology-driven negative taxonomy, not generic hard mining.
min_exp: Add descriptor-mined negatives to MIDOG training; measure FP reduction.

problem: Annotator recall drops in crowded cell fields, biasing detectors against dense regions.
hyp: Modeling label noise as a function of local cell density and reweighting the loss recovers dense-region recall.
why: Density bias systematically undercounts proliferative hotspots.
novel: Structured, covariate-dependent noise model for point annotations.
min_exp: Multi-annotator subset: fit recall-vs-density curve; retrain with correction.
risk: Density estimate circularly depends on detector.

problem: Phase-contrast halo artifacts dominate appearance, hurting cross-microscope transfer.
hyp: Pretraining to invert a physical halo formation model yields features that transfer across microscopes for label-free detection.
why: Label-free imaging avoids staining toxicity in live cultures.
novel: Optics-based inverse problem as pretext.
min_exp: Pretrain halo removal; fine-tune detection on new microscope with 50 labels.

problem: Automated whole-slide mitosis counts disagree with pathologist hotspot-protocol counts, blocking clinical adoption.
hyp: Training a model to first select hotspots as pathologists do, then count, matches clinical grades better than global counting.
why: Grading standards define counting protocol, not whole-slide truth.
novel: Optimizes protocol agreement, not raw detection metrics.
min_exp: Compare grade concordance: protocol-mimicking vs whole-slide counting.

problem: Cell trackers make biologically impossible claims: cells merging, dividing into three.
hyp: Enforcing a binary-division tree constraint jointly over detection and tracking fixes division-event errors.
why: Lineage accuracy is the endpoint for developmental biology.
novel: Hard biological tree constraint inside the tracking objective.
min_exp: Cell Tracking Challenge: division F1 with vs without tree constraint.
risk: Cell death and exit complicate trees.

problem: Nuclear chromatin texture predicts grade but sits below scanning resolution reliability.
hyp: Requiring texture predictions to be consistent under super-resolution/downsampling cycles identifies which chromatin features are real signal versus aliasing.
why: Grading reproducibility across scanners depends on it.
novel: Resolution-cycle consistency as feature-validity test.
min_exp: Dual-resolution scans of same slides; measure feature stability and grade agreement.
risk: True features may be resolution-limited anyway.

problem: Clouds and fog trigger wildfire smoke false alarms in aerial monitoring.
hyp: True plumes stay anchored to a fixed ground source while growing; anchor-point temporal stability separates smoke from advecting clouds.
why: False alarms desensitize dispatch operators.
novel: Physical source-attachment as discriminative temporal feature.
min_exp: HPWREN sequences: anchor-stability feature vs frame CNN on cloud negatives.

problem: Night CCTV flames saturate sensors into white blobs, defeating appearance models.
hyp: Flame flicker (~10Hz luminance oscillation) at saturated-region borders detects fire despite total appearance loss.
why: Night fires spread longest before human report.
novel: Temporal-frequency signature where spatial appearance is destroyed.
min_exp: Night fire clips: flicker-spectrum classifier vs frame CNN on saturated regions.

problem: Smoke appearance differs radically between nadir aerial and oblique CCTV views; models don't transfer.
hyp: Estimating a viewpoint-invariant 3D density proxy, conditioned on camera pose, transfers between aerial and ground cameras.
why: Multi-platform fusion is the operational reality.
novel: Shared volumetric target across heterogeneous camera networks.
min_exp: Train aerial, test CCTV with pose conditioning vs direct transfer.

problem: Visible flame or smoke appears minutes after ignition; earlier optical cues ignored.
hyp: Refractive heat shimmer (local optical-flow turbulence without translation) is detectable in long-lens footage before visible smoke.
why: Minutes of earlier warning change containment outcomes.
novel: Atmospheric refraction as earliest fire signal.
min_exp: Controlled-burn footage: shimmer detector lead time vs smoke detector.

problem: Low sun and haze cause daily rhythmic false-alarm spikes in fixed-threshold systems.
hyp: Modulating detection thresholds by computed sun position and haze estimate flattens the diurnal false-alarm curve without recall loss.
why: Operators disable systems with predictable alarm storms.
novel: Astronomical geometry as explicit covariate, not learned nuisance.
min_exp: Replay month of tower footage; compare alarm-hour distribution and recall.
risk: Overcorrection near dusk suppresses real fires.

problem: Low-bitrate CCTV macroblocking destroys the fine texture smoke detectors rely on.
hyp: Features computed in the codec's DCT domain, which is where smoke energy survives quantization, are robust to compression level.
why: Municipal cameras stream at aggressive bitrates.
novel: Codec-aligned representation instead of pixel-domain robustness training.
min_exp: Recompress benchmark at descending bitrates; DCT features vs pixel CNN.

problem: Steam vents, dust roads, and chimneys alarm daily from the same coordinates.
hyp: Clustering alarms by geo-location across days automatically builds nuisance allow-lists, cutting false alarms without per-camera engineering.
why: Manual masking doesn't scale to thousand-camera networks.
novel: Cross-day spatial recurrence as unsupervised nuisance discovery.
min_exp: Historical alarm logs: allow-list precision and missed-fire audit.
risk: New fires at nuisance sites masked.

problem: Lesion detectors fire outside their host organ; filtering post-hoc discards borderline true positives.
hyp: A differentiable tumor-inside-organ containment loss during training beats post-hoc mask filtering on boundary lesions.
why: Nested structure is universal in oncology imaging.
novel: Containment as training signal, not inference filter.
min_exp: LiTS: containment loss vs post-filtering, stratify by boundary distance.
risk: Organ mask errors propagate into lesions.

problem: One detection head handles lesions whose size and intensity statistics differ per host organ.
hyp: Routing to organ-specific detection heads conditioned on organ context outperforms a shared head at equal parameters.
why: Liver, kidney, lung lesion priors are incompatible.
novel: Anatomical routing, not multi-scale or ensemble stacking.
min_exp: Multi-organ CT lesions: routed vs shared head, matched capacity.

problem: Containment priors assume lesions inside organs, but exophytic tumors bulge outside boundaries.
hyp: Hard containment measurably harms exophytic recall; a soft signed-distance penalty preserves both interior and exophytic detection.
why: Exophytic renal and hepatic tumors are clinically common.
novel: First quantification of the containment-prior failure mode.
min_exp: Stratify KiTS by exophytic ratio; compare hard/soft/no containment.

problem: Global NMS suppresses lesion detections across different organs and merges bilateral findings.
hyp: Running suppression within organ instances (left/right kidney separately) preserves multi-organ and bilateral lesions.
why: Bilateral metastases are prognostically critical.
novel: NMS scoped by anatomical instance hierarchy.
min_exp: Bilateral-lesion cases: recall under global vs organ-scoped NMS.

problem: Unknown whether lesion detectors use lesion appearance or host-organ context, hiding failure modes.
hyp: Inpainting the surrounding organ while keeping the lesion quantifies context reliance; high reliance predicts cross-organ transfer failure.
why: Explains why detectors miss lesions in atypical locations.
novel: Counterfactual anatomical ablation as attribution method.
min_exp: Inpaint organ context on LiTS; correlate score drop with transfer error.

problem: Same metastasis looks different across host organs; per-organ training fragments scarce data.
hyp: Disentangling host-organ style from lesion content lets one detector share lesion evidence across organs.
why: Metastatic patterns span organs; data pooling is essential.
novel: Content-style factorization along anatomical, not domain, axes.
min_exp: Train liver+lung metastases jointly; test held-out organ (adrenal).

problem: Global FROC lets large-organ performance mask failures in small organs like adrenals.
hyp: A per-organ, volume-normalized FROC reveals ranking reversals among published detectors hidden by global metrics.
why: Small-organ lesions are disproportionately missed clinically.
novel: Evaluation reform targeting nested anatomy, with reranking evidence.
min_exp: Re-evaluate three public detectors under both metrics; report reversals.

problem: Chest X-ray L/R markers and technologist tags correlate with portable exams and disease labels.
hyp: Occluding burnt-in markers changes predictions measurably; marker-only crops predict labels above chance, proving shortcut use.
why: Deployment sites use different markers, breaking models silently.
novel: Systematic marker-leakage quantification across public datasets.
min_exp: Marker-crop classifier on CheXpert; occlusion delta per label.

problem: Models should relocate predictions under horizontal flip, but laterality-biased training breaks equivariance.
hyp: A flip-consistency score (prediction mismatch under mirrored input) quantifies laterality shortcut severity per model and per finding.
why: Cheap, label-free audit applicable to any released model.
novel: Equivariance violation as standardized shortcut metric.
min_exp: Score five public CXR models; correlate with external-site drop.

problem: Hemisphere-asymmetry features detect unilateral brain lesions but plausibly miss bilateral, symmetric disease.
hyp: Asymmetry-based detectors show quantifiable recall collapse on bilateral pathology; mixing absolute and asymmetry channels repairs it.
why: Bilateral strokes and toxic encephalopathies are missed at highest cost.
novel: Characterizes the failure mode of a popular prior.
min_exp: Stratify stroke MRI by bilaterality; compare recall curves.

problem: Population-normal models flag benign patient-specific patterns present in both breasts.
hyp: Detecting only asymmetries between a patient's breasts (registered CC/MLO pairs) reduces recalls while keeping cancer sensitivity.
why: Radiologists explicitly compare contralateral views.
novel: Patient-as-own-control detection objective, not population prior.
min_exp: DDSM paired views: asymmetry detector vs single-view baseline recall/specificity.

problem: Mirrored anatomy patients (situs inversus, dextrocardia) reveal whether models memorize anatomical sides.
hyp: Models with strong laterality priors fail catastrophically on mirrored-anatomy cases; a curated benchmark exposes and ranks this brittleness.
why: Rare patients deserve working models; also a purity test for priors.
novel: First mirrored-anatomy robustness benchmark.
min_exp: Curate ~100 situs cases; evaluate public CXR/CT models.

problem: Supine vs prone vs upright positioning changes gravity-dependent findings and correlates with patient acuity.
hyp: Position metadata predicts labels above chance; stratified training removes an unrecognized shortcut, improving cross-position generalization.
why: Portable supine exams dominate ICU, biasing severity labels.
novel: Positioning as a distinct shortcut axis from view or site.
min_exp: Position-only classifier on labels; retrain stratified; test cross-position.

problem: Technologists apply diagnosis-specific window presets (stroke window) only on suspected cases, leaking labels into pixels and metadata.
hyp: A metadata-only classifier on window/level fields achieves nontrivial AUC, and pixel models exploit the same signal.
why: Leakage inflates reported performance invisibly.
novel: Quantifies human-workflow leakage in acquisition parameters.
min_exp: Metadata-only AUC on stroke CT; renormalize windows and remeasure model.

problem: Wrong PixelSpacing tags silently corrupt all size measurements downstream.
hyp: Anatomy with known dimensions (vertebral height, aortic diameter percentiles) detects and corrects implausible spacing metadata automatically.
why: Size thresholds (nodule 6mm) drive clinical decisions.
novel: Self-calibration from anatomical constants at scale.
min_exp: Corrupt spacing on public CTs; measure detection and correction accuracy.

problem: Rescale slope/intercept bugs shift Hounsfield units, silently breaking threshold-dependent models.
hyp: A lightweight probe verifying air/fat/water histogram peaks at canonical HU values catches calibration bugs pre-inference.
why: Silent HU shifts caused real clinical AI failures.
novel: Physics-anchored input validation layer for CT pipelines.
min_exp: Inject slope/intercept faults; measure probe detection rate and model damage prevented.

problem: Private tags, overlays, and scanner signatures let models identify institutions, inflating multi-site cross-validation.
hyp: A site-identification probe quantifies fingerprint strength; performance drops proportionally when fingerprints are scrubbed.
why: Explains reproducibility gap between papers and deployment.
novel: Causal link from fingerprint strength to metric inflation.
min_exp: Train site classifier; scrub tags/borders; remeasure task AUC per site.

problem: Models are forced to be invariant to kVp, contrast phase, and dose, discarding informative acquisition context.
hyp: Feeding acquisition parameters as explicit covariates outperforms invariance training when protocols correlate with anatomy of interest.
why: Radiologists always read protocol context first.
novel: Reverses the default invariance dogma with controlled comparison.
min_exp: Liver lesion characterization: covariate-conditioned vs invariance-trained, cross-protocol test.

problem: Missing or wrong tags (slice thickness, contrast phase) corrupt cohort selection and preprocessing.
hyp: Predicting metadata from pixels and flagging mismatches with recorded tags catches errors reliably enough for automated QC.
why: Research cohorts and federated learning depend on tag correctness.
novel: Pixels audit metadata, inverting the usual dependency.
min_exp: Predict contrast phase on labeled set; audit mismatch cases manually.
risk: Predictor errors create false QC alarms.

problem: PHI pixel scrubbing removes calibration markers, rulers, and image regions models depend on.
hyp: Standard de-identification pipelines measurably degrade detection performance, and damage varies by redaction method, motivating model-aware scrubbing.
why: Every shared dataset passes through de-identification unexamined.
novel: First systematic scrubbing-vs-performance study.
min_exp: Apply three de-id tools to annotated set; compare detector metrics.

problem: Detector anchors and receptive fields tuned on adults mismatch pediatric organ scales.
hyp: Normalizing spatial scale by an estimated body diameter (not pixel count) makes one detector serve neonates through adults.
why: Pediatric data is too scarce for separate models.
novel: Physical patient-size canonicalization, not multi-scale pyramids.
min_exp: Mixed-age CT: size-normalized vs standard anchors, stratify by age.
risk: Size estimate fails on partial fields.

problem: Pediatric growth plates mimic fracture lines, causing adult-trained models to overcall fractures.
hyp: Combining contralateral-limb comparison with age-conditioned physis atlases separates physes from fractures better than appearance alone.
why: Pediatric ED fracture triage is high-volume and error-prone.
novel: Anatomy-development priors fused with within-patient symmetry.
min_exp: Pediatric wrist X-rays: FP rate with vs without atlas and contralateral input.

problem: Normal pediatric thymus reads as mediastinal mass to adult-trained models.
hyp: An age-gated thymus prior (expected size and sail-sign shape by age) eliminates thymus false positives without masking true masses.
why: Thymus is the canonical pediatric false positive.
novel: Explicit developmental-anatomy prior in the detector.
min_exp: Pediatric CXR set: mediastinal-mass FPs before/after thymus prior.

problem: Chronological age poorly indexes development; normal ranges depend on maturation stage.
hyp: Self-supervised biological-age estimation (ossification, organ proportions) modulates normality thresholds better than chronological age.
why: Same-age children vary years in maturation.
novel: Learned developmental clock as conditioning variable.
min_exp: Bone-age set: abnormality detection conditioned on biological vs chronological age.

problem: Pediatric CTs use reduced dose; noise level correlates with age, letting models shortcut age via noise.
hyp: Noise-matched augmentation across ages removes the shortcut, changing pediatric external validation measurably.
why: Confound is universal wherever ALARA dosing applies.
novel: Identifies dose policy as hidden age proxy.
min_exp: Train with noise-matched augmentation; compare age-stratified generalization.

problem: Adult thresholds (cardiothoracic ratio, ventricle size) misfire on children; discrete age bins are crude.
hyp: Learning continuous normative percentile curves over age, GAM-style, gives calibrated abnormality scores across the lifespan.
why: Threshold misuse drives pediatric false positives everywhere.
novel: Growth-chart methodology embedded in imaging models.
min_exp: Fit cardiothoracic normative curves on pediatric CXR; compare flag rates vs fixed threshold.
risk: Normative data skews toward sick children.

problem: Scarce pediatric labels force adult-model reuse, but the transfer mechanism is unexamined.
hyp: Physically rescaling adult scans to child body dimensions during training transfers better than statistical fine-tuning on small pediatric sets.
why: Determines the right recipe for every pediatric application.
novel: Controlled comparison of geometric vs statistical adaptation.
min_exp: Adult-to-pediatric organ segmentation: rescaling augmentation vs fine-tuning at matched label budgets.
